doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jazz repertoire and pointless gigs as director
summary: He programmed jazz, his own pieces and Chucho and Romeu arrangements, but jazz was again imperial music, and the band played mostly useless pub and theater gigs.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What kind of music did you encourage the band to play when you were the director?
Mostly Jazz oriented music, and that was that. Jazz was already again becoming “imperial music”. So, that was not a good idea to play Jazz. You know, the Black Panthers were

not any more around there, so we had nobody else to impress here. So, Jazz is “imperial music”; they didn’t mention that officially, but Jazz was a four letter word again, and all I wanted to do was Jazz oriented music. So, creative music in general, and I didn’t want to do more problem music. And that only lasted one year, until they, in a year they send me home to rest. I was not tired. [Both laugh] I want to rest; rest for what?
Give me an idea of whose music you had the band playing and what tunes you had the band playing.

Wow, that happened so many years ago. I wrote the piece called “Hello to Stano;” and it was a piece dedicated to Stano, for alto, tenor, and big band, that was one piece. Some other pieces by Chucho Valdés, wonderful Afro-Cuban type instrumental music by Chuchos Valdés um, and some arrangements from Armando Romeu that in those days he got a couple of them when they have a big band in the village. That type of music, and some European friends that send me charts, also from Finland, from Sweden, so that was Jazz oriented music.
What kind of gigs did your orchestra play?

A lot of totally useless gigs, you know. Playing in mostly pub things, then they pretended to play my Jazz thing in the middle of a pub gig, you know. In the theater, they have to sing the Italian ballads and things like that. I was trying to be annoying, that’s what it is.
Was it playing mostly what you could call concerts?
The orchestra wasn’t playing clubs, or anything?

No; sometimes we play Tropicana; we play Tropicana, there is a show there, but we didn’t really have a content, demands for that orchestra, because it was a dance orchestra, it was too big also. It was a novelty; it become an oddity, the orchestra.
